The cross-pulsar chromatic fit is diagnostic only because it uses unsigned |H|
amplitudes, includes noise-floor-limited bounding rows, and is strongly limited
by telescope calibration and geometry differences. The fitted free exponent

differences, but with only a few frequency points and large sub-band errors it
is best described as weakly achromatic/inconclusive rather than decisive.

   (Note: Data pre-filtered; all SNR values high. Stratification by percentiles.)

================================================================================
CONCLUSIONS
================================================================================
  • Probabilistic weighting diagnostic gives |H| = 14.159 ns (z = 32.12, not inferential)
  • All 19167 triplets contribute (no data discarded)
  • Bayesian and frequentist weighted diagnostics disagree by 13.681 ns; this supports treating unsigned-|H| as diagnostic only
  • SNR≥5 cut changes the unsigned-|H| diagnostic by 44.488 ns vs. probabilistic weighting

================================================================================
IMPLICATIONS
================================================================================
  1. Hard SNR cuts can systematically bias unsigned-|H| diagnostics
  2. Probabilistic weighting is preferred: no arbitrary thresholds
  3. Full geometric distribution is preserved for diagnostic threshold checks
  4. Low-SNR triplets contribute appropriately to precision
